Depuis le 4 mars 2024, 12 personnes ont: Since March 4, 2024, 12 people have left the Gaza Strip on their own and been authorized to enter Canada. Meanwhile, 986 applications are being processed, meaning they meet all the requirements. And many families are still waiting for codes so they can officially submit their applications.
Le conflit est désormais qualifié de « c: The conflict is now described as a “humanitarian catastrophe.” All the indicators are in the red: the crisis is one of food, health and society. More than 31,000 people have been killed by the Israeli army since October 7, 2023, not counting the Palestinians who have died of starvation or who have been lost under the rubble.
Samar Alkhdour se tient droite avant de: Samar Alkhdour stands up straight before setting down her backpack, which has a sign attached to it that reads: “Day 160 of the genocide in Gaza,” along with the death toll. Among the dead is her daughter Jana, 13, who could not be saved. She was granted permission to come to Canada two weeks after her death.
« J’ai vécu une période très difficile,: “I went through a very difficult time, because I didn’t tell my two children [who are here] about their sister’s passing,” she says, seated and focused on her words. “That was the real suffering for me. My other daughter, who is nine, Shams, would ask me when she saw me filling out documents for my sister: ‘Is that a form for Jana?’” Shams still didn’t know that her big sister had died.
Jana était atteinte de paralysie cérébra: Jana had cerebral palsy and died of malnutrition while she had taken refuge in a church, waiting to be evacuated to Canada. Her mother had been trying to bring her to the country for years.
Arrivée en 2019 au Québec comme demandeu: Having arrived in Quebec in 2019 as an asylum seeker, Samar knows this journey can be difficult.
« J’ai choisi le Canada à l’époque pour: “I chose Canada back then to make my refugee claim because I believed it was a country that valued human rights. Today, I’m disappointed, but I hope that will change,” she says in excellent French, a language she learned in two years in order to integrate into Quebec as quickly as possible.
Samar porte un tableau sur son sac à dos: Samar wears a board on her backpack. Every day, she changes the number of days since the start of the current massacre in the Gaza Strip. She has received a few insults, but believes that more often than not, people give her a thumbs-up in approval. Photo: Adrien Gaertner
Aujourd’hui, Samar s’efforce de sauver s: Today, Samar is doing everything she can to save her sister Siham, who is 28, along with Siham’s husband and their two children. “We’re 10 years apart, and I think of her a bit like my daughter, since I raised her while she was growing up,” says the 38-year-old.
Elle craint que le même sort qui s’est a: She fears that the same fate that befell her daughter will strike her sister.

La Cour internationale de justice (CIJ): The International Court of Justice (ICJ) ruled in January that the State of Israel must prevent and punish acts that could lead to genocide. Since then, international bodies have been called on to rule on the question.

« Nous n’avons rien entendu du Canada, d: “We haven’t heard anything from Canada,” he laments. “It’s the money from the fundraiser that lets us leave Gaza.” The money raised allows six members of his family to leave through the border with Egypt. “I’m still hoping to raise money to get my sister and my brother out,” he says in an online exchange.

« Nous continuerons à suivre la situatio: “We will continue to monitor the situation and work with our partners to support those affected by the crisis who have a connection to Canada. Our current priority is to keep families together and to get them to safety as quickly as possible.”

Or, le problème semble aussi être en amo: Yet the problem also appears to lie further upstream, since more than two months after the program’s launch, many Canadians of Palestinian origin who have submitted an application for their loved ones still have not received a response, or in some cases even a code that would allow them to go further in the process.

Et comme il n’y a pas toujours de réseau: And since there isn’t always an Internet connection in Gaza, she can sometimes go long hours, even more than 24 hours, without news. “Imagine the stress I live with,” she sighs.

Through his press secretary, he said there was “nothing to add” to the response provided by the department.

« Nous utilisons nos fonds pour envoyer: “We use our funds to send weapons to Israel, which is bombing Gaza, an enclave smaller than the City of Laval,” she exclaims.

Selon le programme de visas de résident: Under the temporary resident visa program, it is Canadian families who will have to support their loved ones once they are in the country. Other programs, such as the one devoted to welcoming people displaced from Ukraine by the war, offer more coverage. « Beaucoup de familles canado-palestinie: “Many Canadian-Palestinian families who will welcome loved ones fleeing Gaza are going to need financial help, because they will be responsible for these people for a year,” says Samar. “I think it will be essential to offer psychological support, because people in Gaza went through several attacks even before October 7 [2023].”
Devant des délais qu’ils qualifient de «: Faced with delays they describe as “unreasonable,” lawyers with the Gaza Family Reunification Project are trying to gather enough signatures from family members who feel wronged.
« Nous demandons à la Cour fédérale d’ém: “We are asking the Federal Court to issue an order stating that there has been unreasonable delay and to immediately issue unique reference codes,” reads the online document.
Ce genre de demande est un mandamus, soi: This type of application is a mandamus, a powerful form of legal remedy intended to force immigration authorities, for example, to correct their inaction or unjustified delays in an administrative process. In this case, if Immigration Canada is found at fault, a precise timeline will have to be set by which all responses to visa applications must be delivered.

Alors que l’État hébreu tente d’anéantir: As the Hebrew state tries to destroy Hamas – listed as a terrorist entity by Canada – and to secure the release of 130 Israeli hostages, the international community is seeking to impose a ceasefire in the Palestinian enclave.
Du côté canadien, le 18 mars, les parlem: In Canada, on March 18, members of Parliament voted 204 to 118 on a New Democratic Party (NDP) motion calling for an immediate ceasefire. The original, non-binding motion was amended by the Liberals to remove, among other things, the recognition of a State of Palestine.
La motion exige aussi la suspension de t: The motion also calls for the suspension of all arms trade with Israel and for the government to “ensure that Canadian citizens trapped in Gaza can reach safety in Canada and [to] lift the arbitrary cap of 1,000 temporary resident visa applications.”
Quelques jours après notre entrevue avec: A few days after our interview with Samar, and shortly before the vote on the NDP motion, Immigration Minister Marc Miller announced that he would change the 1,000-application cap on the family reunification visa program. <l1>This change will allow more Gazans with family in Canada to apply under the program</l1>. Despite that, Marc Miller also said that the motion adopted by the Canadian Parliament in favour of a ceasefire and the suspension of exports of weapons of war to Israel <l2>could complicate the departure of Gazans</l2> from the enclave.
